content.overview: Courts dismiss or refuse PILs that cloak private disputes, political rivalries, or publicity-seeking, and may impose exemplary costs for abuse of the liberalised standing rule.
content.study: PIL is a rule of standing, not a new writ. Private disputes dressed as PIL fail. Limits include: no locus for mere busybodies; no PIL for ordinary civil, contractual, or service disputes; restraint where alternative remedies suffice; and refusal of vague or politically motivated petitions. Costs and abuse belong here — courts may award heavy or exemplary costs against petitioners who misuse Articles 32 or 226 under the PIL label.
